name: ArenOmnislash
prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / production JRPG sprite animation. Transform the reference battle sheet into a NEW original ultimate animation atlas of the SAME character. Preserve the reference face, hair, exact clothing, colors, proportions, weapon and detailed hand-drawn pixel-art look. This is authentic 2D pixel sprite artwork, NOT 3D, NOT rendered CGI, NOT vectors. Canvas square. EXACTLY 16 distinct sequential frames in a perfectly regular 4 columns x 4 rows grid, chronological order left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Every cell exactly one quarter of canvas width and height, equal empty transparent gutters. Entire sprite and weapons fit within each cell with at least 8% transparent margins; no artwork crosses cells. Same character size in every frame, boots around 84% down each cell, body centered at x50%, consistent camera and lighting; no scale changes, no zoom. Real transparent alpha background. Character: Aren, spiky blond hair, red scarf and red cape, tan tunic, brown gloves and boots, dark trousers, silver longsword with gold hilt. Faces LEFT in three-quarter side view. An energetic high-level sword limit attack inspired by Cloud's level-four Omnislash, retain Aren's OWN outfit and proportions, not Cloud. Row1 frames1-4: still stance to crouched power-up, hands tightening sword, cape starts lifting, strong wind-up with sword far behind right shoulder. Row2 frames5-8: four progressive poses of a powerful leftward horizontal sword cut, shoulders hips and blade turning together, a short bright gold/silver pixel slash closely following blade. Row3 frames9-12: four progressive poses of an upward diagonal sword cut followed by reverse diagonal slash; twist torso and sweep cape with legwork. Row4 frames13-16: four progressive poses of a downward diagonal slash, rapid cross-cut and balanced follow-through. Keep the body fully readable and consistent; small sword trails only, do not hide him in explosions. Draw actual new poses in all sixteen cells; no walking cycles.
